Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 112, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surat al-Ikhlas

It is Madani.

It is also said: it is Makki.

Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Gather together, and I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and recited to them: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, then he entered his house. He said: The people said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us: "Gather together, and I will recite to you a third of the Qur'an," and he recited: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, then he entered. Is this anything but something [new]? He said: He heard them, so he came out to us and said: "Indeed this surah equals a third of the Qur'an." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from Muhammad ibn Hatim and Ya'qub al-Dawraqi, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from (Yazid) ibn Kaysan... the hadith.

Ismail ibn Abi (Ziyad) narrated from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews entered upon the Prophet of Allah and said: "O Muhammad, describe your Lord for us and tell us His lineage, for He described Himself in the Torah and gave His lineage." The Messenger of Allah trembled until he fell unconscious, and he said: "How do you ask me about the description and lineage of my Lord? Even if you asked me to describe the sun for you, I would not be able to do so." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, descended and said: "O Muhammad, say to them: Allah is the One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He begets not, nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him." That is: He is not a father nor a son, and He has no likeness among His creation.

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This hadith was related to us by the Shaykh al-'Afif Abu 'Ali ibn Bandar in Hamadhan, with its chain, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad... the hadith.

And in some reports: Surat "Say: O you who disbelieve" and Surat "Say: He is Allah, the One" are the two "al-Muqshqishatan", meaning they clear one of shirk and hypocrisy. It is said: "qashqasha" describes the sick person when he recovers from his illness. The surah is called Surat al-Ikhlas because it contains nothing but the description of the Lord by His name, and it contains no command, prohibition, promise or warning.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi mentioned in his book, through the narration of Abu Ja'far al-Razi from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the polytheists said: "O Messenger of Allah, give us the lineage of your Lord," so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He begets not, nor is He begotten﴾, because there is nothing born except that it will die, and there is nothing that dies except that it will be inherited, while Allah does not die and is not inherited. ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾. He said: There is no likeness to Him and no equal, and nothing is like Him.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, meaning: say, He is Allah the Wahid (the One), with "Ahad" in the sense of "Wahid." It has been distinguished between "al-Ahad" and "al-Wahid."

It is said: "al-Ahad" is more emphatic than "al-Wahid." It is said: "So-and-so is not contested by anyone (ahad)," as a negation of the whole, whereas it is said: "He is not contested by one (wahid)," and it is possible that two may contest him. Also, "wahid" may be the one followed by a second and third in number, whereas "ahad" cannot carry this meaning. Most of the exegetes hold that it means "wahid."

As for His words ﴿Huwa﴾ at the beginning, there is an implicit noun in it, as if it points to the fact that the one you asked me about is Allah the One. So His words ﴿Allah, the One﴾ are an explanation and clarification of the implicit pronoun in His words ﴿Huwa﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 112, verse 2:

As for His saying: ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad)﴾, there are several opinions. The first: He is the One to whom one turns (yasmudu ilayhi) for needs. The second: He is the One who has reached the utmost in lordship (al-su'dud, nobility and sovereignty) and attained its perfection.

The poet said:

(Ala, let the bearer of news bring good tidings to the Banu Asad, [of the death] of Umar, and Ibn Mas'ud, and the lord al-Samad.)

Another said:

(I struck him with a sword, then I said to him: "Take it, Hudhayfah, for you are the lord, the Samad.")

The third opinion: He is the One who has no hollow (jawf), meaning He does not eat. The fourth opinion: its explanation is His saying: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten﴾. It was also said: He is the Everlasting who does not perish, and it was said: He is the Enduring who does not cease.

He said: ﴿He neither begets nor is born﴾, meaning: He has no father and no son.

It was also said: this is a negation of the claim of the Jews and Christians that ʿUzayr is the son of God, and that the Messiah is the son of God, and a negation of the claim of the polytheists that the angels are the daughters of God.

All of this is concerning His words ﴿He neither begets﴾.

As for His words ﴿nor is He born﴾, it contains a negation of the claim of the Christians that Mary, peace be upon her, gave birth to a god, namely the Messiah.

And His saying: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ means: no one was an equal to Him, nor a likeness. It is in the order of inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) as we have mentioned, and the meaning of "one" (ahad) at the end of the surah is other than the meaning of "one" (ahad) at the beginning of the surah.
